text: Every NG message is a cookie, one space, then a bencoded dictionary; over WebSocket one frame carries exactly one message.
notes: request and reply framing on UDP, TCP and ws; replies accepted in binary or text frames

text: Over TCP the messages follow each other on the byte stream with no extra delimiter; the reader parses one cookie and one bencode value at a time.
notes: replies split across segments reassemble; corrupt or oversized streams (over 4 MiB, cookie over 256 bytes) drop the connection

text: Over UDP a message is one datagram; a body that does not fit a datagram needs the TCP or WebSocket transport.
notes: requests over max_datagram (default 65507) or refused with emsgsize return {error, too_large}; 30 KB offers and replies pass

text: The cookie is unique per request and the reply carries the cookie of the request it answers.
notes: distinct cookies per command; concurrent callers each get the reply for their own request; unknown cookies are dropped

text: A request without a reply is retransmitted byte-identical with the same cookie; the daemon serves a duplicate cookie from its reply cache.
notes: UDP retransmits reuse the cookie; the fake models the cookie cache; attempts exhausted give {error, timeout}

text: Over reliable transports a request is sent once; only the deadline applies.
notes: ws and tcp send once and time out after attempts * timeout

text: Every reply has a result: ok or pong on success, error with error-reason, load limit when the daemon sheds load; a warning may accompany a successful result.
notes: ok/pong -> {ok, Reply} with warning kept; error -> {error, Reason, Reply}; load limit -> {error, load_limit, Reply}

text: Bencode is canonical: dictionary keys are unique and sorted as raw strings, integers have no leading zeros and no negative zero, string lengths have no leading zeros.
notes: encoder sorts keys and refuses duplicate keys; decoder rejects non-canonical integers and length prefixes

text: A decoder bounds what a peer can make it do: nesting deeper than 64 containers is refused.
notes: chappe duty: 64 levels decode, 65 return too_deep

text: Command dictionaries use the documented key names (call-id, from-tag, media address, ICE-lite, T.38, ...) and flag names as listed in the protocol documentation.
notes: atom keys map to the documented names; option words hyphenate, other atom values go verbatim; floats and tuples are refused before sending

text: A call is created by offer (or publish), completed by answer and removed by delete, all keyed by call-id and from-tag; the from-tag is always the tag of the party sending the offer.
notes: session lifecycle, callee re-INVITE tag swap, delete on stop or owner death even with a request in flight, node down and restart notices

text: Only one offer/answer exchange is open per call at a time.
notes: chappe duty: a competing offer returns {error, glare}; a rejected re-INVITE rolls back with reoffer_rejected/1

text: A node addressed by name may move; the client follows the name to its current address.
notes: chappe duty: tcp and ws resolve on every connect; udp re-resolves every resolve_interval_ms (default 60000) and after resolve_after_timeouts consecutive timeouts (default 2), swapping the destination (and the socket when the family changes)
